en: A Praise of the Ultimate Truth: How shall I praise you, O Protector, who are unarisen and without abode?
It transcends worldly analogies and lies beyond the range of the path of speech.
Nevertheless, however you may be—the range of experience regarding the meanings of suchness—I shall praise the Guru with devotion, relying upon worldly convention. (2)
Since you possess the nature of the unarisen, no arising exists for you;
O Lord, there is neither going nor coming—homage be to you who are non-existent. 3.
You are neither existence nor non-existence, neither annihilation nor eternal;
you are neither permanent nor impermanent—homage be to You, the non-dual! 4.
For indeed, not even a single color—green, madder-red, yellow, white, or black—is perceived in you; homage be to you who are beyond all color.
You are neither great nor small, neither long nor circular;
you have attained the state beyond all measure—homage be to you, the immeasurable! (6)
Salutations to you who abide nowhere— not far away nor yet near, not in space nor on earth, neither in saṃsāra nor in nirvāṇa.
Not abiding in any phenomena, you have reached the course of the realm of phenomena;
having attained supreme profundity, homage be to you, the Profound One! (8)
If he is praised when thus praised, let him be praised; or rather, what indeed is praised?
Since all phenomena are empty, who is praised or by whom is he praised? (9)
Who is able to fully praise you, who are devoid of arising and passing away, for whom there is neither end nor middle, and in whom neither the grasped nor the grasper exists? (10)
Having praised the Sugata, who has neither gone nor come and is free from all movement, may this world, by that merit, proceed toward the state of the Sugata. (11)
